# Step 3 - Digitally Sign the OTP Request XML

## Goal

Before sending the OTP Request XML to the Aadhaar Authentication Server, the XML **must be digitally signed** using the certificate issued for your AUA/Sub-AUA.

The digital signature ensures:

* The request was generated by an authorized organization.
* The XML has not been modified during transmission.
* The sender can be authenticated.

---

## Prerequisites

Before signing the XML, ensure you have:

* A valid OTP Request XML generated in **Step 2**.
* A valid signing certificate (P12/PFX or as provided by your organization).
* The corresponding private key.
* The certificate password.
* An XML Digital Signature (XMLDSig) library supported by your programming language.

---

## Signing Workflow

```text
Generate OTP Request XML
            │
            ▼
Load Signing Certificate
            │
            ▼
Load Private Key
            │
            ▼
Generate XML Digital Signature
            │
            ▼
Embed Signature into XML
            │
            ▼
Signed OTP Request XML
```

---

## XML Before Signing

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>

<Otp
    uid="999988887777"
    ac="public"
    sa="public123"
    lk="MKQ8R2XXXXXXXXXXXXXX"
    txn="OTP202607161530001"
    ts="2026-07-16T15:30:00"
    ver="2.5"
    ch="00">
</Otp>
```

---

## XML After Signing

After signing, the XML will contain a **`<Signature>`** element.

Example:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>

<Otp
    uid="999988887777"
    ac="public"
    sa="public123"
    lk="MKQ8R2XXXXXXXXXXXXXX"
    txn="OTP202607161530001"
    ts="2026-07-16T15:30:00"
    ver="2.5"
    ch="00">

    <Signature xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#">
        ...
    </Signature>

</Otp>
```

> The actual contents of the `<Signature>` element are generated automatically by the XML Digital Signature library. You should not create or modify this element manually.

---

## Signing Checklist

Before proceeding to the next step, verify the following:

* The XML is well-formed.
* The digital signature has been successfully added.
* The signing certificate is valid and not expired.
* The private key matches the certificate.
* The XML remains valid after signing.
* The `<Signature>` element is present.

---

## Common Errors

| Error                        | Possible Cause                                     |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Certificate not found        | Incorrect certificate path or missing file         |
| Invalid certificate password | Wrong password for the P12/PFX file                |
| Private key not available    | Certificate does not contain the private key       |
| Signature generation failed  | XMLDSig library configuration issue                |
| Certificate expired          | Renew the certificate before signing               |
| XML modified after signing   | Any modification invalidates the digital signature |

---

## Security Recommendations

* Store certificates securely.
* Never expose the private key in source code.
* Never commit certificate files to version control.
* Restrict access to the signing certificate.
* Rotate certificates according to your organization's security policy.

---

## Output of this Step

At the end of this step, you should have a **digitally signed OTP Request XML** that is ready to be transmitted to the Aadhaar Authentication Server.

The next step is:

**Step 4 – Send Request**

---

## Notes

> Do not modify the XML after it has been digitally signed. Even a small change, such as adding a space or changing an attribute value, will invalidate the signature.

> Always use the signing certificate issued for your AUA/Sub-AUA environment (Sandbox or Production).

> The digital signature provides authenticity and integrity of the request. It does not encrypt the XML.
